crags.name: Index Town Wall
crags.notes: Granite dries fast. Lower Wall sheds water quickly; Upper Wall slower after heavy rain.

crags.name: Leavenworth
crags.notes: Rain shadow effect — dries significantly faster than west-side crags. Icicle Canyon blocks moisture.

crags.name: Vantage
crags.notes: Desert climate, basalt dries fast. Wind is a major factor — often climbable when west-side crags are soaked.

crags.name: Little Si
crags.notes: Wetter microclimate than Index. Higher humidity typical. Needs more drying time.

crags.name: Mt. Erie
crags.notes: Island climate — high humidity, slow drying. Needs 48h+ after rain to be reliable.

crags.name: Peshastin Pinnacles
crags.notes: Sandstone — NEVER climb when wet. Holds water in pockets, damages rock when damp. Needs 48-72h after rain.

crags.name: Exit 38
crags.notes: Closest sport climbing to Seattle. Metamorphic andesite dries slower than granite. Many walls face north or are shaded by forest — factor in extra drying time. Deception Crags is most popular; Far Side and Mt Washington have longer approaches.

crags.name: Castle Rock
crags.notes: Southwest-facing granite in Tumwater Canyon. Gets afternoon sun, dries reasonably fast. Home to Washington's first multipitch technical rock climb (Midway, 1948). Rock is polished from heavy traffic — friction matters more when damp.

crags.name: Smith Rock
crags.notes: High desert volcanic tuff dries fast and the climate is much drier than PNW. Often climbable year-round. Watch for seasonal raptor closures (Feb-Aug on some walls). Juniper Basin area dries fastest.

crags.name: The Chief
crags.notes: The big one. Massive south-facing granite wall — beautiful in good conditions but very slow to dry due to size and coastal moisture. Seeps can persist for days after heavy rain. Upper Chief dries slower than the base. Check the access society for any closures before heading up.

crags.name: Smoke Bluffs
crags.notes: The local's playground — lower elevation, well-traveled, and significantly faster-drying than The Chief. Often climbable a day after rain clears when the Chief is still weeping. Varied aspects mean some walls see sun most of the day. One of the best urban crags in North America.

crags.name: Miller River Boulders
crags.notes: Deep forest setting, slow drying. 6 sub-areas: Morpheus, Paradise, Prospect, Hideout, Jungle Gym, Apex. 205 problems. Needs significant dry time after rain.
